name: Slave
overview: Scripture provides detailed instructions regarding the treatment and rights of slaves, emphasizing both justice and mercy. For example, an Hebrew servant was to serve six years and then be set free without payment, highlighting the provision for eventual freedom. The law strictly forbids kidnapping and selling a man, prescribing death for such acts, and mandates punishment if a servant is mistreated to the point of death. Additionally, if a servant is injured, such as losing an eye, he must be released as compensation, underscoring the value of their well-being. The ownership of bondmen and bondmaids from surrounding nations is also regulated, reflecting the social order established in the Mosaic law.
